input.rationale: Section 4(c) is the only effects-of-termination provision and it addresses just cessation of Services, revocation of the license, Customer's cessation of use, and mutual return-or-destruction of Confidential Information (at the holder's election). There is no obligation for Kubient to return AP's data (Content, Requests or other data it collects, maintains or stores under section 8(iii)) in a usable format, no export deadline, no certified deletion, and no wind-down or transition assistance anywhere in the Agreement. In a hosted auction-platform arrangement this falls below even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days), so we insert the preferred transition and data-return language into section 4(c).

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return in machine-readable format, and certified deletion into the effects-of-termination clause.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added an orderly exit: up to six months of transition assistance at Kubient's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. As drafted, section 4(c) lets Kubient simply stop the Services and destroy material with no obligation to hand our data back; we can accept a 90-day assistance period as a fallback.

ops.text: (v) at Customer's request, Kubient will provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months following such termination or expiration at Kubient's then-current rates; and (vi) within thirty (30) days of such termination or expiration, Kubient will return to Customer, in a commonly used, machine-readable format, all Content, Requests and other Customer data then in Kubient's possession or control, and will thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing.
